title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All directors, officers and other key management personnel of the Company, and any other person nominated by the Chairman or Company Secretary. Subject to closed periods, prior written clearance and the 'Other prohibitions' in Part 5 (third-party financial products; limiting economic risk of unvested entitlements).

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chairman or the Company Secretary may specify additional periods when Designated Persons are prohibited from trading, including during periods when the Company or its subsidiaries are involved in the drilling or testing of exploration wells; these are added to the 'prohibited periods'. The policy does not state whether the existence of such an additional period is disclosed or kept confidential.

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban with no clearance route: Designated Persons cannot deal at any time in options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over the Company's Securities by third parties such as banks. An OTC put or call written by a bank over Karoon shares falls squarely within this. Only exception is where the Company's Securities are a component of a listed portfolio or index product.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products such as options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over the Company’s Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.

rules.detail: Separate, specific ban on entering transactions in products associated with the Company's Securities that limit the economic risk of unvested entitlements.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into transactions in products associated with the Company’s Securities which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company over unvested entitlements (eg hedging arrangements).

rules.detail: Section 5.2 only names unvested entitlements, but any hedge structured as a third-party financial product (an OTC put/call with a bank) over vested shares is independently and absolutely prohibited by section 5.1's blanket ban on third-party financial products, regardless of vesting state.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products such as options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over the Company’s Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar structure with a bank is a 'financial product ... issued over the Company's Securities by third parties' and so falls within the absolute ban.
rules.evidence: or other financial products issued over the Company’s Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named and is not addressed by the narrow 'apply for, acquire or dispose' dealing definition.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
A CFD referencing the Company's shares is a financial product issued over the Company's Securities by a third party, caught by the same absolute ban as other bank-issued derivatives.
rules.evidence: not permitted to deal at any time in financial products such as options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over the Company’s Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.

rules.detail: Entering into a margin loan is not addressed; the policy only carves a lender's forced sale under such an arrangement out of the closed/prohibited period restrictions (see exceptions and financing).
Granting a charge, lien or pledge over Securities is not named, and is not caught by the narrow dealing definition (apply for, acquire or dispose of Securities, or agree to do so).
No provision addresses entering into secured financing generally; only a forced-sale carve-out for secured lenders exists (see exceptions and financing.forced_sale_in_closed_period).
No holding period, intention test or short-term dealing restriction is stated anywhere in the policy.

requirements under a court order or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements;

a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending agreement;
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer;

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back ... including ... the sale of entitlements required to provide for the take up of the balance of entitlements under a renouncable pro rata issue

the exercise (but not the sale of Securities following exercise) of an option or right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a prohibited period and the Company has been in an exceptionally long prohibited period or the Company has had a number of consecutive prohibited periods
trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this policy

exemption_authority: The Notification Officer may give prior written clearance to trade during a prohibited period only in exceptional circumstances (hardship, court order, or other circumstances determined by the Chairman/CEO) under 4.1, but this exceptional-circumstances process applies to the closed-period/clearance regime in Part 3, not to the absolute ban on third-party financial products in 5.1, which has no stated exemption or waiver route at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products such as options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over the Company’s Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions. An exception may apply where the Company’s Securities form a component of a listed portfolio or index product.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a standalone, unconditional prohibition (not merely a Dealing requiring clearance) that squarely covers a bank-written OTC put and call over Karoon shares, and unlike the closed-period regime it has no exceptional-circumstances or clearance override, so a funded collar cannot be structured under this policy regardless of vesting state or timing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into transactions in products associated with the Company’s Securities which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company over unvested entitlements (eg hedging arrangements).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if 5.1's absolute ban were read narrowly, this separate clause independently blocks any hedge of unvested holdings, confirming a collar can only ever be contemplated (subject to 5.1) over vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending agreement, is excluded trading and may be undertaken at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a lender could ever hold security (which 5.1 does not directly forbid but the derivative ban makes moot for a collar), its enforcement sale would not itself breach the closed-period rules, though entering the security arrangement is otherwise unaddressed by the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairman or the Company Secretary may specify additional periods when Designated Persons are prohibited from trading including during periods when the Company or its subsidiaries are involved in the drilling or testing of exploration wells.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For an exploration company these ad hoc blackouts can be frequent and of undefined length, adding timing risk to any entry, roll or unwind of a collar structure even where one were otherwise permitted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the period from the close of trading 10 days before the Company’s annual general meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The lodged text does not state when this closed period ends, creating uncertainty as to open-window timing for any dealing (including collar execution) around the AGM.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 5.1 imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on Designated Persons dealing 'at any time' in options, warrants or other financial products issued over the Company's Securities by third parties such as banks -- a category that squarely captures an OTC put and call written by a bank -- and this prohibition has no clearance mechanism, exceptional-circumstances process or other exemption route. Section 5.2 separately and independently bans any product limiting the economic risk of unvested entitlements. The policy is silent on entering secured financing or granting security over shares generally (it only excludes a secured lender's forced sale from closed-period restrictions), so the loan leg is not itself prohibited, but this is moot given the outright ban on the derivative legs. Even the ordinary dealing/clearance regime (14-day closed periods, written Notification Officer clearance, 14-day permission validity) would not rescue the structure, since 5.1 sits outside and is not subject to that clearance process at all.
